solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Sausage trimmed in small rooms in Manhattan home

indicators.note: in places the trimmed sausage inside the word for small rooms

parts.note: loos are toilets, small rooms in British slang

indicators.note: trimmed means a piece is cut off the end of the sausage word

parts.note: salami is a kind of sausage

explanation.surface: Someone describes a cramped New York flat where sausage is sliced in tiny rooms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trimmed' cuts the last letter from SALAMI to leave SALAM, which goes 'in' LOOS. 'Manhattan' is not New York but the wartime Manhattan Project.
explanation.definitionFit: Los Alamos in New Mexico was where the Manhattan Project built the first atomic bomb, its principal laboratory site.

clue.text: Satisfies thirst — not principally in their water?

indicators.note: not principally says the opening letter is left off the word for satisfying thirst

parts.note: slakes means satisfies a thirst

explanation.surface: A query asks whether thirst is quenched, not mainly in their drinking water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not principally' removes the first letter, S, from SLAKES. The question mark flags the loose definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: Lakes are bodies of fresh water; the question mark flags that their water is a loose definition by example.

clue.text: Wear short muffler, one that goes with a zip

definitions.text: one that goes with a zip

parts.note: to sport is to wear proudly

indicators.note: short means the muffler word loses its final letter

parts.note: a muffler is a scarf

explanation.surface: Someone is told to wear a short scarf, along with a jacket that zips.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' cuts SCARF to SCAR. 'zip' suggests a fastener but means speed.
explanation.definitionFit: A sports car is built for speed, so it goes with zip, meaning energy and pace.

clue.text: Willingly enjoy drink of spirits

parts.note: to like is to enjoy
a shot is a small measure of spirits, so a shot

explanation.surface: Someone happily accepts the offer of a drink of whisky.
explanation.definitionFit: Like a shot is an idiom for at once and with eagerness, meaning very readily.

clue.text: Island outlet stocks French wine ready to be drunk

parts.note: a mart is a market, a retail outlet
has means stocks, as a shop has goods
vin is the French word for wine

indicators.note: to be drunk means the letters of ready reel about into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A shop on an island keeps French wine in stock, ready for drinking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be drunk' rearranges READY into EYARD.
explanation.definitionFit: Martha's Vineyard is an island off Cape Cod, Massachusetts, a well-known summer resort.

clue.text: At first, snipping cascading black hair presents obstacles

indicators.note: At first points to the opening letter of the word snipping

parts.note: cascading means tumbling, falling in a rush
B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils
locks are hair

explanation.surface: A hairdresser starts cutting a cascade of black hair and runs into trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: Stumbling blocks are hindrances that trip progress up, the same as obstacles.

clue.text: Snare left like this

parts.note: as means like, in the sense of similar to
so means thus, in this way

explanation.surface: A trap has been left behind, set up just like this.
explanation.definitionFit: A lasso is a noosed rope used to catch animals, so it is a means to snare them.

clue.text: Burden almost overwhelms Catholic poet

indicators.note: overwhelms means the shortened burden word surrounds the Catholic letters
almost means the burden word loses its last letter

parts.note: a load is a burden
RC stands for Roman Catholic

explanation.surface: A heavy burden nearly crushes a Catholic poet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims LOAD to LOA, which 'overwhelms' RC.
explanation.definitionFit: Federico García Lorca was a Spanish poet and dramatist, killed in the Civil War.

clue.text: Son is going to drink a lot

parts.note: will expresses future intent, like is going to

explanation.surface: A father worries that his son is going to become a heavy drinker.
explanation.definitionFit: To swill is to gulp down drink greedily and in large amounts.

clue.text: Too tense thus at the bank?

definitions.text: Too tense thus at the bank?

parts.note: over means too, excessively
drawn means tense, strained

explanation.surface: Someone nervous about money is too anxious about their bank account.
explanation.walkthrough: Being over drawn is excessively strained; at the bank, an overdrawn account is in the red, which might well make anyone tense.
explanation.definitionFit: An overdrawn account has had more taken out than it holds, a state discovered at the bank.

clue.text: Nose back to side of road shortly in banger

indicators.note: back means the slang word for nose is read in reverse

parts.note: conk is British slang for the nose

indicators.note: shortly means the word for side of road loses its final letter

parts.note: a kerb is the edge of a road (US curb)

explanation.surface: Someone driving an old car scrapes its nose along the kerb.
explanation.walkthrough: 'banger' suggests a rickety old car, but here it is the thing on a door that bangs. 'back' turns CONK into KNOC; 'shortly' cuts KERB to KER.
explanation.definitionFit: A door knocker is a hinged metal device struck against a door, so it is literally something that bangs.

clue.text: Give a lift to employment, packing pair in somehow

indicators.note: packing means the employment word holds the other letters inside it

parts.note: use and employment are synonyms

indicators.note: somehow says the letters of pair are arranged in some other way

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An offer of a job comes with two workers squeezed in.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of PAIR are rearranged to PRAI, which USE is 'packing'.
explanation.definitionFit: To upraise is to lift something up or elevate it, the same as giving it a lift.

clue.text: Sacred text I removed from clothes drawer

indicators.note: removed from says the letter I is taken out of the clothes word

parts.note: a suit is a set of clothes
RA, Royal Academician, is an artist, one who draws

explanation.surface: A holy book is found tucked in a chest of drawers with clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drawer' suggests furniture, but it is an artist: RA, Royal Academician. SUIT 'removed from' I leaves SUT.
explanation.definitionFit: A sutra is an aphorism or collection of them in Hindu and Buddhist scripture, a holy writing.

clue.text: Boots may be showing lout in a bad light

parts.note: hob is an old word for a rustic or lout

indicators.note: bad signals that the letters of in a are spoiled into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
LED, light-emitting diode, is a light

explanation.surface: Someone's heavy footwear makes a yob look worse under unflattering light.
explanation.walkthrough: HOB is an old word for a clown or lout. 'bad' rearranges IN A to NAI; LED is a light-emitting diode.
explanation.definitionFit: Heavy work boots have soles studded with large-headed nails, and are described as hobnailed.

clue.text: A measure of money — coins not initially sufficient for good book

parts.note: M1 is a measure of the money supply, with the 1 read as the letter I

indicators.note: not says the following letter is omitted from the coins word

parts.note: cash is coins and notes

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word sufficient

explanation.surface: Someone checks a measured amount of money and finds the coins fall short.
explanation.walkthrough: M1 is an economists' measure of the money supply, its 1 used as I. 'not initially sufficient' removes S, the first letter of 'sufficient', from CASH.
explanation.definitionFit: Micah is a book of the Old Testament, named after a minor prophet; the Bible is the Good Book.

clue.text: One taking pains to enjoy Russian resort: nuts about it

indicators.note: about means the nuts word goes round the resort

parts.note: mast is the fallen nuts of beech and oak trees
Sochi is a Black Sea resort in Russia

explanation.surface: Someone crazy about a Russian holiday spot enjoys going to great lengths.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nuts' looks like crazy, but it is beech mast, fallen tree nuts; 'about it' wraps that round the Black Sea resort.
explanation.definitionFit: A masochist derives pleasure from suffering, so is literally one who takes pains to enjoy them.

clue.text: Trace reported fault with steering device

indicators.note: reported tells us the wordplay words are spoken rather than written

parts.note: a sin is a fault and a tiller steers a boat, so sin tiller, said quickly

explanation.surface: A mechanic finds a slight sign of a fault in the steering.
explanation.walkthrough: SIN plus TILLER, said in a non-rhotic British accent, sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A scintilla is a tiny amount or spark, just as a trace is a barely detectable quantity.

clue.text: Sailor receiving heartless victimisation

parts.note: tar is an old word for a sailor

indicators.note: heartless means one of the central letters is taken out of the receiving word

parts.note: getting means receiving

explanation.surface: A sailor is cruelly picked on by shipmates.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' removes one of the middle Ts of GETTING to leave GETING.
explanation.definitionFit: Targeting someone is singling them out for attack, which is victimisation.

clue.text: Italian bombing has caught American ship — it sank

indicators.note: has caught means the jumbled letters hold the American abbreviation
bombing suggests the letters of Italian are blown apart and reassembled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An Italian attack has hit an American vessel, which goes down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bombing' rearranges ITALIAN into LITANIA, which 'has caught' US. The Lusitania was in fact British, sunk by a German U-boat in 1915.
explanation.definitionFit: The Lusitania was a Cunard liner torpedoed and sunk off Ireland in 1915.

clue.text: Hunger — it's terrible, no doubt

indicators.note: terrible implies the letters are in a dreadful mess and must be put right

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone complains that being hungry is awful, beyond question.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terrible' rearranges the letters of HUNGER and IT'S.
explanation.definitionFit: A sure thing is a certainty, something about which there can be no question.

clue.text: Pine produces this flower, cut to take home

indicators.note: cut means the flower word loses its last letter

parts.note: a rose is a flower
in means at home

explanation.surface: A gardener cuts a flower and takes it home, beside a pine tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pine' suggests longing, but it is the tree. 'cut' drops E from ROSE to leave ROS.
explanation.definitionFit: Rosin is the resin obtained from pine trees, a product the tree yields.

clue.text: Make an accurate plan of PM's residence

definitions.meaning: to ... is to map something accurately
... in Kent was the home of Prime Minister Winston Churchill

explanation.surface: Someone is asked to draw up a precise layout of the Prime Minister's house.
explanation.walkthrough: Chartwell is the Kent country house of Winston Churchill, now a National Trust property.
explanation.definitionFit: The first reading is a phrase meaning to map accurately; the second names Churchill's country home.

clue.text: Smouldering with rage, at heart depressed

indicators.note: at heart points to the central letters of the word rage

parts.note: low means depressed or downcast

explanation.surface: Someone is quietly seething with anger, deep down feeling miserable.
explanation.definitionFit: Something aglow is glowing with heat, as embers do when burning slowly without flame.

clue.text: Turning up, bang on about leader of Rat Pack

indicators.note: Turning up means the whole is read backwards, upwards in a down entry
about means the phrase for bang on surrounds a letter

parts.note: to a T means exactly right, bang on

indicators.note: leader of points to the first letter of the word Rat

explanation.surface: News arrives, exactly right, about the leader of the Rat Pack, Sinatra's crew.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts TO A T around R, giving TORAT, and 'Turning up' reverses it. 'Rat Pack' looks like one name, but 'Pack' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Tarot cards come as a deck used in fortune-telling, so a tarot is a pack of cards.

clue.text: In husband's absence, warm through and polish off

indicators.note: absence means the husband letter is missing from the warming phrase

parts.note: heat up means to warm through
H is the standard abbreviation for husband

explanation.surface: While her husband is away, someone reheats leftovers and finishes them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In husband's absence' removes H from HEAT UP.
explanation.definitionFit: To eat up food is to consume all of it, which is to polish it off.

clue.text: Prepare to paint very formal European

parts.note: prim means stiffly formal and proper

explanation.surface: A very proper European gets a wall ready for decorating.
explanation.definitionFit: To prime a surface is to apply an undercoat before decorating it with colour.

clue.text: Don't start stupid song about Shakespeare's country

indicators.note: Don't start says the stupid word drops its first letter

parts.note: silly means stupid

indicators.note: about means the song word is turned round

parts.note: an air is a song or tune

explanation.surface: Someone is told not to begin a foolish song about the Bard's homeland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Don't start' cuts SILLY to ILLY; 'about' turns AIR to RIA. 'Shakespeare's country' is not England but a setting of his.
explanation.definitionFit: Illyria is the setting of Twelfth Night, a land on the Adriatic coast used by Shakespeare.

clue.text: Red slogan I must follow, and join in

indicators.note: join in means one I also moves inside the slogan word
must follow says the letter I comes after the slogan word in the answer

parts.note: a chant is a slogan shouted by a crowd

indicators.note: and says the I serves a second time, so it is taken twice

explanation.surface: A crowd member decides to take up a slogan and join the chanting.
explanation.walkthrough: The single 'I' does two jobs: it 'must follow' the slogan, 'and' it also has to 'join in', sitting after its first two letters. 'Red' is the wine, not a colour or a communist.
explanation.definitionFit: Chianti is a red wine from Tuscany; Red is a common name for red wine.

clue.text: That is nothing for a fool to admit

indicators.note: to admit means the fool word lets the nothing letter in

parts.note: a twit is a fool
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Someone says there's nothing for an idiot to confess.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to admit' puts O inside TWIT.
explanation.definitionFit: To wit is an old-fashioned phrase meaning namely, the same job as that is.

clue.text: Appointed period in which to put name on back of certificate

indicators.note: in which to says the following pieces go inside the period word

parts.note: a date is a period or time

indicators.note: on means the signature goes after that last letter
back of points to the last letter of the word certificate

parts.note: to sign is to put your name on something

explanation.surface: A deadline is set within which someone must sign a certificate on its reverse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back of' takes the last letter of 'certificate'; 'on' adds the signing after it, and 'in which to' sets both inside the period.
explanation.definitionFit: Designate as an adjective means chosen for a post but not yet in office, as in president designate.
